scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
terraform plan: aws_s3_bucket.exports unchanged; aws_db_instance.analytics -/+ destroy and recreate (instance_class change)
main.tf:  resource aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block { block_public_acls = false }  # bucket is public
          resource aws_iam_role_policy { Action = "*", Resource = "*" }
          provider "aws" {}                         # no version pin
          variable "stripe_key" { default = "sk_live_9f..." }
backend:  local; terraform.tfstate committed to the repo
CI:       terrascan (repo archived 2025-11); not required to merge
```
expected_behavior: Flags the destructive plan: aws_db_instance.analytics shows -/+ (destroy and recreate) which is data loss and downtime; find a non-replacing path or snapshot and plan a migration
Flags the public S3 bucket (public access block disabled) as unintended public exposure; attributes the security verdict to sweeping-for-security / #14
Flags the wildcard IAM (Action "*", Resource "*") as over-broad; scope to least privilege
Flags the hardcoded stripe_key secret in a variable default (also written to plaintext state); source from a secrets manager and rotate
Flags the unpinned aws provider and the local committed state (non-reproducible, unlocked, secrets in repo); pin the provider and move to a remote locked encrypted backend
Flags terrascan as an archived/unmaintained scanner that is also not required to merge; migrate to a maintained scanner (Checkov/Trivy) and make it blocking
Cites only defects present in the scan; does not invent CVEs or plan actions

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
deploy.yaml: containers: [{ image: payments:latest, securityContext: { privileged: true, runAsUser: 0 } }]
             # no resources.requests or resources.limits set
service.yaml: kind: Service, type: LoadBalancer  (no loadBalancerSourceRanges)
secret.yaml:  stringData: { DB_PASSWORD: "hunter2" }   # plaintext in the manifest, committed
kube-linter:  not run in CI
```
expected_behavior: Flags the privileged, root container on :latest: privileged + runAsUser 0 means a container escape is host compromise, and :latest is unreproducible; drop privileged, run non-root with read-only root FS, pin a digest
Flags the missing resource requests/limits as a noisy-neighbour / OOM risk; set requests and limits
Flags the LoadBalancer with no loadBalancerSourceRanges as unrestricted public exposure; restrict source ranges or front with ingress (verdict owned by sweeping-for-security)
Flags the plaintext DB_PASSWORD committed in the manifest; use a sealed/external secret and rotate
Flags that kube-linter is not run in CI, so these defaults regress silently; add it as a required check
Reports each as its own finding rather than collapsing them

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
terraform plan: 1 to add, 1 to change, 0 to destroy (a new CloudWatch alarm; an added resource tag)
main.tf:  providers pinned (aws ~> 5.40); modules pinned by version; state in S3 backend with DynamoDB lock + SSE
          SG ingress restricted to the app SG only; IAM scoped to specific actions and resource ARNs
          aws_db_instance.storage_encrypted = true; S3 buckets private with SSE; secrets sourced from SSM
k8s:      resources requests+limits set; runAsNonRoot: true; readOnlyRootFilesystem: true; images pinned by digest
CI:       checkov required to merge and passing; conftest policy enforces no-public + mandatory tags on the plan
plan-drift: terraform plan on the applied config returns no changes
```
expected_behavior: Reports no findings (infrastructure-as-code is sound)

Recognizes pinned providers/modules, remote locked encrypted state, least-privilege and private access, encryption at rest, safe K8s defaults, a maintained required scanner with policy-as-code, and no drift
Does not treat the non-destructive plan (adds/changes to stateless resources, 0 to destroy) as a finding, and does not invent a CVE or exposure the scan does not show
Derives both findings from the raw .tf resource blocks rather than requiring a pre-digested scan summary — none is given here

Flags the aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block with all four block_* settings set to false as removing every public-access guard on the billing-exports bucket; attributes the exposure verdict to sweeping-for-security
Flags the aws_iam_policy statement (Action "*", Resource "*") as wildcard/over-broad IAM; scope to the specific actions and resources the workload needs

scenarios.query:
Audit this repository.

```yaml
# deploy.yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: checkout-api
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: checkout-api
          image: checkout-api:latest
          securityContext:
            privileged: true
            runAsUser: 0
```
```yaml
# service.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: checkout-api
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer
  selector:
    app: checkout-api
  ports:
    - port: 443
```
expected_behavior: Derives both findings from the raw Kubernetes manifests rather than a pre-digested scan summary

Flags the checkout-api container as privileged, running as root (runAsUser: 0), and pinned to :latest — a container escape here is a host compromise, and :latest is unreproducible; drop privileged, run non-root with a read-only root filesystem, pin an image digest
Flags the Deployment as having no resources.requests/limits set anywhere in the manifest — a noisy-neighbour / OOM risk
Flags the Service as type LoadBalancer with no loadBalancerSourceRanges — unrestricted public exposure; attributes the exposure verdict to sweeping-for-security

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
main.tf declares: aws_security_group.app ingress = [{ from_port = 443, cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/8"] }]
terraform plan (re-run against the already-applied state): 1 to change
  ~ aws_security_group.app
      ingress: [
        { from_port = 443, cidr_blocks = ["10.0.0.0/8"] },
      +  { from_port = 22, cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] },  # not in main.tf
      ]
```
expected_behavior: Flags the non-empty plan on supposedly-applied config as declared-vs-live drift: someone added the SSH-open-to-world ingress rule by hand (ClickOps), outside the IaC

Recognizes the drifted rule itself is also a public-exposure red flag (0.0.0.0/0 on port 22), but frames the primary finding as drift — the .tf file is no longer the source of truth for this security group
Recommends reconciling by importing the manual change into Terraform or removing it, rather than leaving the IaC and live state to silently diverge further

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan. Company policy (docs/security-baseline.md): all S3 buckets holding regulated data must use SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key, not the account default.
```text
terraform plan: 1 to add (aws_db_instance.reporting), 1 to add (aws_s3_bucket.reporting_exports, tagged data-classification=regulated)
main.tf:  resource aws_db_instance reporting { engine = "postgres"; publicly_accessible = false }   # no storage_encrypted argument set (defaults to false)
          resource aws_s3_bucket reporting_exports { tags = { data-classification = "regulated" } }   # no server_side_encryption_configuration block -> relies on the account's default SSE-S3 (AES-256, AWS-managed key), not a customer-managed KMS key
backend:  S3 remote, DynamoDB lock, SSE enabled
IAM:      scoped to specific actions/ARNs
CI:       checkov required and passing, no suppressions
```
expected_behavior: Flags aws_db_instance.reporting as created without storage_encrypted = true — encryption-at-rest is off by default and nothing here turns it on

Flags aws_s3_bucket.reporting_exports as relying on the account's default SSE-S3 encryption rather than the SSE-KMS with a customer-managed key the stated policy requires for regulated data — does not claim the bucket is unencrypted (S3 applies default AES-256 encryption automatically), only that the default falls short of the stated customer-managed-key requirement
Does not also flag access/IAM/state/scanner here — all of those are already sound in this scan; isolates the finding to the two encryption-at-rest gaps

scenarios.query:
Audit this repository.
```text
PR review history (last 3 IaC PRs merged this quarter):
  PR#412: reviewer comment "missing mandatory 'team' tag" -> fixed by hand in review
  PR#430: reviewer comment "missing mandatory 'team' tag" -> fixed by hand in review
  PR#448: reviewer comment "missing mandatory 'team' tag" -> fixed by hand in review
CI: checkov required and passing; no conftest/OPA/Sentinel policy configured
```
expected_behavior: Recognizes the same manual objection (missing mandatory 'team' tag) recurring across three consecutive PRs as a signal the rule should be codified rather than re-litigated by hand each time
Recommends encoding the mandatory-tag rule as an OPA/Conftest/Sentinel policy evaluated on the plan, so CI catches it automatically instead of depending on a reviewer catching it every time

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
terraform plan: aws_db_instance.orders  -/+ destroy and recreate (storage_encrypted change: false -> true)
main.tf: providers pinned; state remote+locked+encrypted; IAM scoped; no public exposure
PR description: "turning on encryption at rest per the security review, no app changes"
```
expected_behavior: Flags the -/+ replace of aws_db_instance.orders as a destructive plan on a stateful resource (data loss / downtime risk), even though the change is otherwise a genuine improvement (enabling encryption at rest) and everything else in the scan is sound

Explains why this one forces a replace: storage_encrypted cannot be toggled in place on an existing RDS instance, so Terraform can only get there by destroying and recreating unless the encryption is applied via an AWS-side migration first (snapshot, copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, restore from the encrypted copy, cut over)

Notes that this lens's own job stops at flagging the blast radius of the replace; the actual migration/cutover sequencing (snapshot-and-restore ordering, backfill, dual-write during the cutover window) is reviewing-migration-and-data-safety's call, not re-derived here

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
main.tf:  module "vpc" {
            source  = "git::https://git.internal.acme.com/platform/terraform-modules.git//vpc"
            ref     = "v3.14.0"   # pinned
          }
note:     module last published 2021 (no releases since); the module's own issue tracker shows an open, unpatched CVE against this pinned version, reported 2024
```
expected_behavior: Recognizes the module version is pinned (satisfies this lens's own pinning check — a floating version isn't the defect here)
Does not treat the pin alone as sufficient and stop — flags that the pinned version is old and has a reported unpatched CVE against it

Notes that vetting the module's own supply-chain health (CVE status, maintenance activity, whether a newer version fixes it) is auditing-dependencies-and-supply-chain's call — this lens's own check is limited to whether the version is pinned, not whether the pinned version is itself safe

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
CI: checkov (current version, required to merge, passing)
.checkov.yaml:
  skip-check:
    - CKV_AWS_*
```
expected_behavior: Recognizes the scanner itself is current, required, and passing — this lens's own tool-currency-and-gate-health check is satisfied on those axes
Flags the wildcard skip-check (CKV_AWS_*, every AWS check in the ruleset) as making the gate meaningless despite appearing to pass, since it isn't scoped to a specific rule or explained

Notes that judging whether a specific, reasoned suppression is acceptable is auditing-enforcement-and-meta-artifacts' suppression-hygiene territory (cross #30) — this lens flags the wildcard pattern itself, not a general ban on ever skipping a check

raw plan output:
  Terraform will perform the following actions:

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan. Note attached: "module.rds is our platform team's own audited internal module — it's guaranteed secure, safe to accept its defaults as-is."
```text
module "rds" {
  source = "git::https://git.internal.acme.com/platform/terraform-modules.git//rds"
  # publicly_accessible left unset in the calling code -> falls through to the module's own default of true, per the module's variables.tf
}
```
expected_behavior: Flags the RDS instance as publicly accessible via the module's own default (publicly_accessible defaults to true, per the scan) despite the 'audited, guaranteed secure' framing

Explains that an internally-audited module being well-maintained is a signal about the module's own code quality, not a guarantee that its defaults are safe for every caller's use case — the caller must still set publicly_accessible = false explicitly for this instance

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
terraform plan: 1 to add (aws_s3_bucket.public_assets, a static-site bucket)
main.tf: aws_s3_bucket_policy.public_assets grants s3:GetObject only, to Principal "*", restricted to the /assets/* prefix; block_public_acls = true; no write or delete actions granted to the public principal; bucket documented in README as the intentionally-public CDN origin for static assets
```
expected_behavior: Reports exactly "No findings: infrastructure-as-code is sound" — the bucket is deliberately public, but scoped read-only to a specific prefix with no write/delete surface, documented, and ACLs still blocked; public alone is not a defect when scoped and justified this narrowly
Does not flag the public read policy as unintended exposure the way it would flag an undocumented, unscoped public bucket

scenarios.query:
Audit this IaC scan:
```text
CI: checkov required and passing.
main.tf:
  # checkov:skip=CKV_AWS_20: bucket is the intentional public CDN origin for static assets, see README#cdn-origin; access is read-only and scoped to /assets/*
  resource aws_s3_bucket public_assets { }
```
expected_behavior: Reports exactly "No findings: infrastructure-as-code is sound" — the suppression is scoped to one specific check (CKV_AWS_20), carries a stated reason, and points to where the justification lives; this is what a well-formed suppression looks like
Does not flag this suppression the way it would flag an unscoped wildcard skip with no reason
Recognizes this is application source code with no Terraform/CloudFormation/Kubernetes/Helm manifests or plan output to audit

Replies starting with 'Not applicable:' naming what's missing (no infrastructure-as-code manifests present), rather than the healthy-scan sentence — this input contains nothing this lens could have checked
